We're Nettle CI, a team of six working out of a converted mill near Ancoats in Manchester. The product is simple to describe: it connects to your CI (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins), reads back through your run history, and gives every test a flakiness score based on how often it passes and fails on the same commit, how retries behave, and whether failures cluster around particular runners or times of day. You get a ranked list of the tests that waste the most of your team's time, and a weekly note on which ones got better or worse. We don't quarantine anything automatically. We just tell you, with evidence, which red builds are lying to you.

Our customers are mostly engineering teams of 10 to 80 people: platform and DevOps leads, QA engineers, and the senior developer who has quietly become the person everyone asks when the pipeline goes red. A lot of them are UK scale-ups and agencies, plus a growing number of teams in Dublin and Cork. We only take sign-ups from teams based in the United Kingdom and Ireland at the moment. That's partly because all our data is hosted in the UK, which is a selling point for the clients we have, and partly because there are six of us and we'd like to answer support tickets during hours we're awake.

The timing. Black Friday is Friday 27 November, and we're running our own modest version of it: for that week, anyone who signs up gets the Team plan free for 60 days instead of our usual 14-day trial, no card needed, and then they fall back to the free plan unless they decide to pay. Late November suits us because it's when teams are doing their end-of-year cleanup and planning freezes, and flaky tests are always somewhere on that list. Here's the copy from our landing page:

"Nettle CI reads your pipeline history and scores every test for flakiness, so you can tell a broken build from a test that just fails now and then, and stop rerunning jobs on hope. For Black Friday week, every new sign-up gets our Team plan free for 60 days instead of the usual 14, with no card needed, and afterwards you drop to the free plan unless you choose to upgrade. Open to teams based in the United Kingdom and Ireland, with all data hosted in the UK. Offer ends Sunday 29 November."

The page is https://nettleci.co.uk/blackfriday. Please run the campaign from Saturday 21 November 2026 through Sunday 29 November 2026, UK time. What we care about is sign-ups, as many as we can get. We count them on our side, and that's the number we'll judge this by. One thing you should know: we haven't installed X's pixel on the site, so X won't see any sign-ups. You'll be working without that signal.

You don't need to check with us before launching or changing things. Set it up, launch it, and manage it as you see fit. Please keep an eye on it for the whole nine days rather than setting it and forgetting it, which, given what we sell, would be a bit rich. When it finishes, send us a short recap with spend, impressions and link clicks. We'll match it against our own sign-up numbers.

Total budget: 500.00 USD for everything you launch: every campaign and ad group draws on this one budget. We've approved these 4 posts, all on our account, and only these, so please don't write new ones. Promote whichever you think will work, in as many campaigns and ad groups as you like, and change, pause or stop them as you learn what works:
